name: open-late-closed-released

graded_by.test: owed by the core plan for the open-shell bound — the core waits the target's bound plus one heartbeat_interval toward a worker below 0.6 too, and a channel_opened after it gave up is closed and released with nothing recorded

description: A channel_opened arrives after the core gave up waiting for it (ipc-control open_shell, release; session-open steps 12 and 14). The core's wait for channel_opened, the target's bound plus one heartbeat_interval, applies toward every worker: toward a 0.5 worker the open_shell carries no open_timeout, the worker applies no bound, and the core waits the same. The wait expires, which nothing on this socket shows; then the worker's channel_opened arrives. The core never offered the session, so it closes it with close_channel, and on the channel_closed by: core that answers it sends release, so the worker drops the session instead of listing it until its connection closes. The core records nothing for it: no session record, no recording, no audit line. If the worker wrote a spool entry for the session (it ended the channel by itself, or saw the target close it, before the close_channel reached it), the core deletes that entry before it sends release, auditing nothing; that is a file operation, which this socket does not show. A 0.6 worker racing its own bound is answered the same. The core's wait and its answer to the late open are graded by U2's test.

messages.note: toward a 0.5 worker: no open_timeout, so the worker applies no bound; the core still waits the target's bound plus one heartbeat_interval, and that wait expires after this line: nothing crosses the socket when it does
late: the core gave up on this open and never offered the session
nothing to record: no session record, no recording, no audit line; the session's spool entry, if any, was deleted first with nothing audited; the worker drops the session from its manifest
